intro: What this realm relies on when it relies on somebody else's certificate. Every use case goes through one validation door; this page shows what that door holds each one to, the certificate authorities it may reach, and what is pinned.
paranoidNote: auto is on in product mode and off in development. While it is in force each use case below is held to the full checks; a use case switched off, or every use case while it is not in force, behaves as it did before paranoid PKI mode existed, and nothing else changes.
phase: enforced at its sites from rollout phase {phase}
signersNote: The certificate authorities, and the intermediates under them, a third party's certificate may chain to when it is relied on for anything but a TLS handshake. This list is this realm's own. A leaf never goes here: a leaf to pin goes on the entry or relationship that uses it.
fileSet: {file} gave {n} of the entries below (pki.signerTrustAnchorsFile, default realm only).
emptySigners: This realm's signer truststore is empty.
addNote: Paste one or more PEM certificates. A self-signed CA becomes an anchor and any other CA an intermediate, which must chain to an anchor held. Each refusal is named.
addPurposes: Trust them only for these use cases (none ticked means every use case):
addAccept: Accept this one server certificate by name, for outbound TLS only. It is still held to its validity and fields, and to any revocation list it names.
pinsNote: Every certificate this realm relies on because somebody registered it, held to the checks whatever the settings above say. Last audited: {when}.
emptyPins: Nothing pinned has been audited in this realm.
clientNote: A different store: the {n} anchor(s) a TLS client certificate is verified against at a handshake. It is the process's, not this realm's, because a handshake has no realm in it.
